## Authentication
Session Token (csrf-token) — Authentication method detected from captured traffic.

### Providing credentials
- Prefer passing auth as request headers or cookies at call time (do not hardcode secrets into the skill).
- If executing via an external proxy/executor, pass per-call credentials (cookies and/or headers) so they are not persisted.

## Dependencies
- Runtime capable of HTTPS requests.
- If using `scripts/api.ts`: TypeScript toolchain (or transpile to JS).

## Endpoints

### Data Read (3)
- `GET /api/v1/snippets/websites/{websiteId}/cookies` — Retrieve cookie information for a specific website.
- `GET /attribution_trigger` — Retrieve attribution trigger data.
- `GET /resource-blocker/i18n/en.json` — Get the English language resource blocker configuration.

### Data Write (2)
- `POST /api/v1/snippets/websites/{websiteId}/statistics` — Submit website statistics.
- `POST /v1/websites/{websiteId}/cookie-consent` — Submit cookie consent information for a website.

### Config (1)
- `GET /getconfig/sodar` — Retrieve the SODAR configuration.

### Core API (1)
- `POST /wa/` — Submit a web accessibility (WA) request.

```typescript
  "cookies_accepted": true,
  "timestamp": Date.now()
};

console.log("Cookie consent submitted successfully.");
```

## About This Skill

This skill provides access to Ncsl's internal API — the hidden endpoints that power their web/mobile app.
These are NOT official public APIs. They were captured by observing network traffic while using the site.

**Important:**
- Auth tokens in `auth.json` may expire — re-capture if you get 401 errors
- Internal APIs can change without notice — endpoints may break
- Rate limits are unknown — be conservative with request frequency

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when you need to:
- Access Ncsl data without official API access
- Automate actions on www.ncsl.org (faster than browser automation)
- Call the same endpoints the Ncsl frontend uses
